solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Project close to failure: sacking may come from it

parts.note: to project is to stick out, or jut

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A venture on the brink of collapse, with staff layoffs looming as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacking' looks like dismissal from a failing project; it is the coarse cloth woven from this fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Jute fibre is woven into hessian, the coarse cloth used for sacks.

clue.text: Tar over grass, constructing pool

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, as is a jack (Jack Tar)
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Laying tarmac over a lawn to build a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' and 'grass' look like building materials but are slang for a sailor and cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is an accumulated pool of prize money, as in a lottery or card game.

clue.text: Painter I brought in to supply bathroom fitting

indicators.note: these letters are carried into the middle of the others

parts.note: a well is a source of supply, as of water or information
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An artist is hired to provide a fixture for the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts, so it is a stock crossword painter; 'supply' is a noun here, a source such as a well.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel rail is a bar fixed to a bathroom wall for hanging towels.

clue.text: Peer at home drinking tea, forming attachment to hunter?

indicators.note: the pair of words takes the tea inside, between them, as if swallowing it

parts.note: to peer is to look closely, or watch
someone at home is in
cha is a British slang word for tea

explanation.surface: A nobleman sits at home sipping tea while becoming fond of a fox-hunting horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunter is also a pocket watch with a hinged cover protecting the glass, so the 'attachment' is the chain securing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter is a pocket watch with a lid, and a watch chain fastens such a timepiece to a waistcoat.

clue.text: Pop up and see doctor: being collected

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: pa and pop are both words for father
lo is an old word meaning look or see
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Dad pops in to visit the GP while getting picked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being collected' suggests being fetched; it means being composed.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-possession, the state of being calm and collected under pressure.

clue.text: Eccentric graduate taking in cricket match in unlikely place?

parts.note: an eccentric is a cam, the off-centre wheel turning rotation into to-and-fro motion

indicators.note: the degree holder takes the match inside

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
ODI stands for one-day international, a form of cricket match

explanation.surface: An oddball graduate attends a cricket game somewhere you would never expect one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' reads as an adjective but is a noun, the engineering term for a cam. Cambodia is no cricketing nation, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a Southeast Asian country with no cricket tradition, an improbable venue for an international match.

clue.text: Qualification time given by race official

indicators.note: the qualification and time come next to, beside, the race

parts.note: to career is to rush along at high speed
a diploma is a qualification awarded on completing a course

explanation.surface: A competitor's qualifying time, issued by the official at a racing event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' is a verb here: to career.
explanation.definitionFit: A career diplomat is a professional official in the diplomatic service, rather than a political appointee.

clue.text: Side motorists adopt left of imaginary line

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motorists' organisation
a cricket or football side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Drivers keep to the left-hand edge of a road marking.
explanation.walkthrough: The imaginary line is an axis, and axial means relating to one.
explanation.definitionFit: Axial describes something relating to or around an axis, the notional line an object turns about.

clue.text: Drama introduces Harry: touching figure!

indicators.note: the drama comes first, leading in what follows

parts.note: Noh, also spelt No, is classical Japanese drama
to harry is to pester, or nag
on can mean touching, as in resting on

explanation.surface: A play brings on Prince Harry, a poignant character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching figure' reads as a moving character, but 'figure' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a geometric figure, a polygon with nine sides.

clue.text: Reason for going to press witness: he's worn out

indicators.note: out here means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A witness is exhausted from facing journalists, and is pressed for a reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn out' looks like one phrase meaning tired, but 'worn' is part of the fodder and 'out' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsworthiness is the quality that justifies printing a story, the reason it gets published.

clue.text: Brief corporation on railroad, maybe, that's to go round Jersey?

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another comes after it, so the trimmed corporation follows

parts.note: to railroad someone is to bully or coerce them, and to cow is one example of that

indicators.note: a brief version is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a large paunch, a belly

explanation.surface: A short note about a company operating a railway, and something circling the island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective on the company, but it trims BELLY, the paunch sense of 'corporation'. Jersey is not the island but a breed of dairy cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jersey is a breed of cow, and a bell hung on a collar around its neck lets herders locate it.

clue.text: Alien craft, one commandeered by humans

indicators.note: something commandeered is taken over and held, so these letters are enclosed by the humans

parts.note: man means humankind, humans as a whole
craft as in skill is art
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial spaceship, one of which has been hijacked by people.
explanation.definitionFit: A Martian is a supposed inhabitant of Mars, the stock alien of science fiction.

clue.text: Kid to make relay race a bit shorter?

definitions.meaning: to kid is to tease or fool someone

definitions.text: to make relay race a bit shorter?
definitions.meaning: read literally, to tug on one stage of a relay to shrink it

explanation.walkthrough: A relay race is run in stages called legs, so pulling one of them could whimsically shorten the race.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull someone's leg is the idiom for teasing or kidding them.

clue.text: Pour from this running water through milk dispenser

indicators.note: the river runs through the middle of the dispenser, so its letters sit inside

parts.note: a teat is the nipple from which an animal's milk is dispensed
the Po is Italy's longest river, running water

explanation.surface: A tap's flow runs into a dairy machine, and you pour from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running water' suggests a tap; it is a river, the Po.
explanation.definitionFit: A teapot is the vessel from which brewed tea is poured into cups.

clue.text: Soreness from multiple blows to the face?

definitions.text: Soreness from multiple blows to the face?

parts.words: Soreness from multiple blows to the face?
parts.note: the blows sound like punches but are gusts of wind striking the skin

explanation.surface: Pain left by being punched repeatedly in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blows' suggests a beating, but here it means the wind blowing hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Windburn is skin irritation and redness caused by exposure to strong, cold gusts.

clue.text: Not having used sheets until pens deployed

indicators.note: deployed means moved into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bedding goes unused until writing instruments are put to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheets' suggests paper alongside pens; it means bedclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed that is unslept-in has not been used for sleeping, so its sheets remain fresh.

clue.text: Formally request private to be new recruit?

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly, a request made in a formal phrase such as 'I beg to differ'
inner means private, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: Asking officially for a soldier to be enlisted as a fresh recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' reads as a soldier among recruits; it is the adjective, INNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner is a novice, someone newly started, like a fresh recruit.

clue.text: Feverish, tearful end to supplicant's squirming

indicators.note: squirming is wriggling about, so these letters are jumbled
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A tearful petitioner writhes at the close of a desperate plea.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of 'supplicant' is T, which joins TEARFUL in the mix before 'squirming' rearranges the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflutter means in a nervous, excited state, much like being in a fever of agitation.

clue.text: Tango in a bit, you understand — now resting

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the rest
something you understand is heard rather than seen, so the words sound like what is entered

parts.note: a bit is a piece, said aloud as 'a piece'
T is Tango in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Dancing the tango for a while, you see, and now taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At peace' is a euphemism for dead, now resting.
explanation.definitionFit: At peace is a gentle euphemism for someone who has died and is now at rest.

clue.text: Works quietly to stop old habits

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so this letter is put inside the others

parts.note: uses can mean customs or habitual practices
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Quietly working to break long-standing bad habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habits' is not monks' robes but customs, USES.
explanation.definitionFit: Opuses are artistic works, especially musical compositions, numbered in a catalogue.

clue.text: Unit on the house becoming loose

parts.note: a set is a unit, a group of things forming a whole
something on the house is given free

explanation.surface: A unit of accommodation offered free, and it is coming loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' is a verb here, to release.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose something is to release it, the same as setting it free.

clue.text: Girl, on reflection, regretted one-woman shows

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters are read backwards
the letters show within the words, so they are hidden there

explanation.surface: A woman, thinking back, regrets her solo stage performances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' looks like thinking it over; it signals reading backwards in 'regretted one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Odette is a woman's given name, famously the swan princess of Swan Lake.

clue.text: Still in fear of returning, remains in American park

parts.note: petrified means both turned to stone, still, and frozen with fear

indicators.note: the word goes back the way it came, so it is read backwards

parts.note: the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: Someone still frightened of going back stays where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The Petrified Forest National Park in Arizona is famous for fossilised logs turned to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrified Forest is a US national park in Arizona, preserving ancient trees fossilised into quartz.

clue.text: Closed trailers bring hoppers

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed
trailers are advertisements for films, ads

explanation.surface: Shut-up caravans attract grasshoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailers' suggests vehicles; it means film previews, ADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Toads move by hopping, so they are hoppers.

clue.text: Ace crippled in battle

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
lame means disabled in the leg, crippled

explanation.surface: A star pilot was wounded during combat.
explanation.definitionFit: El Alamein in Egypt was the site of decisive Second World War battles in the North African desert.

clue.text: One raising a glass kitchen appliance

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from toast: a person drinking someone's health, and the device for crisping sliced bread.

clue.text: Bed of roses with trees, as yet to be replanted

indicators.note: trees that are replanted are set out anew, so the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A rose bed alongside trees that have yet to be moved to new ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed of roses' looks like gardening, matching the trees, but it is the idiom for a comfortable life.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy street and a bed of roses are both idioms for a life of comfort and ease.

clue.text: Begging, one puts one's cap on the floor?

definitions.text: Begging, one puts one's cap on the floor?

parts.words: Begging, one puts one's cap on the floor?
parts.note: a beggar lays a hat on the ground for coins, but the cap meant is the bony one on a leg joint, lowered when pleading

explanation.surface: A beggar sets their hat on the pavement to collect money.
explanation.walkthrough: The cap is the kneecap: someone begging drops to their knees, putting that bone's cap down.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint covered by the kneecap is what a pleading person rests on the ground when kneeling.
